A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRD study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-extraction experiments in Section 5 and Appendix A, including downstream-task performance, safety alignment, watermark resistance, scaling, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their reported numerical and graphical outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same response selection, cold-start substitution, objective, and regularization. Algorithm 1 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same twelve datasets and six task categories described in Section 5.1 and Table 9. Appendix A retains the same translation languages and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MLE in Tables 1–3 and 7, grey-box KD in Table 2, and direct-prompting SimPO in Table 4. The added citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The query budgets, model configurations, metrics, training settings, and testing procedures are retained throughout Section 5 and Appendix A. Tables 1 and 2 still use 16 translation queries and 64 QA queries, respectively.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the same watermark-resistance, query-efficiency, model-scaling, distribution, loss-ablation, and direct-prompting analyses. No analytical question or experimental case is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five training repetitions with means and variability in Section 5.1. Tabular uncertainty reporting and plotted uncertainty bands are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings match across both versions. For example, Table 2 retains PIQA accuracy of 0.785±0.01 for LoRD and 0.760±0.02 for MLE; Appendix A's experimental pages are visually identical apart from page numbers.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–2, the query-complexity argument, mathematical definitions, and Appendix B's derivations and proofs are retained without substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about alignment-consistent extraction, query efficiency, watermark resistance, and downstream performance.

C2.justification: The preference-overfitting explanation, exploration–stability tradeoff, and task-difficulty interpretations are unchanged. The limitations concerning multimodal models, resources beyond LaViSH, and lower-level extraction are also retained.

D1.justification: The code link, Table 8 prompts, Table 9 dataset/checkpoint links, pseudocode, and implementation details are unchanged. Both versions report the same learning rate, sequence lengths, hardware, and LoRD hyperparameters.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zheng et al. (2019), Xiao et al. (2022), and Zhang et al. (2025) in the introduction, plus Liang et al. (2025a,b) in Appendix C. It briefly places prompt extraction outside the related-work discussion; the existing research positioning otherwise remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 revises the author/affiliation block, adds contact information and a corresponding-author designation, and inserts acknowledgments. Introduction and related-work additions are limited; the core prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from PDF page 3 to page 4, Table 1 receives minor formatting changes, and text reflows around the additions. The same eleven figures and nine tables remain, with unchanged graphical content and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly expands bibliographic context and adds author/contact and funding information. Its method, proofs, experimental evidence, interpretations, and substantive limitations remain unchanged. The brief scope clarification and limited formatting edits leave overall evidential strength and explanatory quality essentially unchanged.
